I think the best placement would be:

I think I'll go with both placements—one in the action bar to reduce friction early on, and one in the export area at download time. Now I'm thinking through what the badge should look like.

Designing the badge with a checkmark icon, "ATS-Friendly Formatting" text, and a green success color scheme to keep it compact and non-intrusive. I'll position it below the Export PDF button in the export area when a formatted document exists, and also add it as a small badge below the Format button in the action bar for maximum visibility. Now I'm placing the trust badges in two strategic locations - adding the ATS-friendly indicator next to the Export PDF button in the export area, and also inserting a small hint below the Format button in the action row so users see the reassurance before they commit to formatting.

Placing the badges... I'm settling on a two-part approach: adding a compact ATS-Friendly badge in the export area that only appears when there's a formatted document ready, and placing a static indicator in the action bar below the Format button to keep the messaging consistent throughout the interface.

gh pr create --title "feat(FRG-274): add ATS-Friendly badge and callout near download" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- Adds a **"✅ ATS-Friendly" pill badge** in the export header area, displayed alongside the Export PDF button once a document has been formatted
- Adds a **"✅ ATS-Friendly Formatting — works with all major applicant tracking systems"** callout in the action bar below the Format button, acting as a persistent trust signal for users before they submit

## Motivation
Users searching for resume formatting have anxiety about ATS compatibility. Explicitly calling it out near both the primary CTA (Format button) and the download action (Export PDF) removes friction and reinforces confidence at the two most critical moments in the user journey.

## Changes
- `pages/index.vue`: Added `.ats-badge` element (shown when `formattedXml` is set) in the export area, `.ats-callout` paragraph in the action bar, and corresponding scoped CSS for both

## Test plan
- [ ] Load the app at `/` — confirm the `.ats-callout` text is visible below the "Format My Resume" button
- [ ] Paste sample content and click Format — confirm formatted document appears
- [ ] Confirm "✅ ATS-Friendly" badge appears in the header next to Export PDF
- [ ] Verify neither element appears in print/PDF output (both are inside `.no-print` containers)
- [ ] Verify build passes (`npm run build`) ✅

Closes FRG-274

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"

## Status
DONE

## What Changed
- `pages/index.vue`: Added `✅ ATS-Friendly` pill badge in the export header area (visible when a document is formatted, next to Export PDF button) + `✅ ATS-Friendly Formatting — works with all major applicant tracking systems` callout in the action bar below the Format button; added `.ats-badge` and `.ats-callout` scoped CSS styles

## Key Decisions
- Placed the trust signal in **two locations**: the action bar (persistent, seen before formatting) and the export header (seen at download time) — covers both moments where ATS anxiety is most likely to arise
- The header badge is conditionally shown (`v-if="formattedXml"`) so it only appears alongside the enabled Export PDF button; the action bar callout is always visible as a pre-submit trust signal
- Both elements live inside `.no-print` containers, so they won't bleed into the exported PDF

## PR / Branch
- Branch: `feature/frg-274-ats-friendly-badge`
- PR: https://github.com/kimwwk/ohmydoc-using-claude-code-agent/pull/46
